title: CODATA 2022 does not mark the vacuum magnetic permeability as exact
summary: NIST gives μ₀ as 1.256 637 061 27 × 10⁻⁶ N A⁻², standard uncertainty 0.000 000 000 20 × 10⁻⁶. The relative standard uncertainty is 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁰.
body:
The NIST page 'CODATA Value: vacuum magnetic permeability', for the 2022 recommended values, opened 2026-11-18, prints the numerical value 1.256 637 061 27 × 10⁻⁶ N A⁻². The standard uncertainty is 0.000 000 000 20 × 10⁻⁶ N A⁻². The relative standard uncertainty is 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁰. The concise form on the page is 1.256 637 061 27(20) × 10⁻⁶ N A⁻². The page does not mark the value exact.

BIPM's list of seven defining constants does not include the vacuum magnetic permeability. This card does not reconstruct what μ₀ was before 20 May 2019, because that earlier exact status was not on the pages opened for this card. What those pages do show is that, in the 2022 adjustment, μ₀ carries a stated uncertainty.

sources.title: The International System of Units (SI): Defining constants
sources.author: Bureau International des Poids et Mesures
sources.note: Page opened 2026-11-18. BIPM dates the fixed values to the revision that took effect on 20 May 2019 and cites CGPM Resolution 1 (2018).
